subject: E-Commerce
title: The De Minimis Loophole
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The De Minimis Loophole.

hook.text: The US allows $800 worth of imports per day duty-free. Chinese sellers exploit this to ship billions tax-free.

buildup.text: De minimis rules were designed for travelers bringing personal gifts. They weren't built for modern e-commerce.

discovery.text: Temu and Shein ship millions of small packages, each under $800, directly to US consumers. Duties: $0.

twist.text: US lawmakers are pushing to close the loophole. If it shuts, prices on Temu and Shein would rise dramatically.

climax.text: An outdated trade rule became the backbone of a billion-dollar discount shopping revolution. Policy drives commerce.

punchline.text: $800 duty-free per package. An old travel rule powers Temu's entire business.

quiz.question: What is the 'de minimis' threshold in US imports?
